pages.name: Back from a rise
pages.text: The [[original]], the amount before a change, is always 100%. £180 after a 20% rise is 120% of it, so divide by the multiplier, 1.2, to go back. 180 ÷ 1.2 = £150.

pages.name: Before a rise
pages.task: After a 15% rise, a load draws 46 A. What did it draw before?
pages.why: 46 A is 115% of the old load, so divide by 1.15. 46 ÷ 1.15 = 40 A, and 40 × 1.15 = 46 checks it. The rise was 15% of 40 A, which is 6 A.

pages.name: Back from a cut
pages.text: A cut goes back the same way. 25% off leaves 75%, so a cable run cut to 90 m was 90 ÷ 0.75 = 120 m. Going back from a cut gives more.

pages.task: A tool costs £68 after 15% off. What did it cost before?
pages.why: 15% off leaves 85%, so £68 is 85% of the old price. 68 ÷ 0.85 = £80, and 80 × 0.85 = 68 checks it. Going back from a cut gives more.

pages.name: Which sum?
pages.task: A £300 price has 20% added on. Which sum gives the price before?
pages.why: £300 is 120% of the price before, so divide by 1.2. 300 ÷ 1.2 = £250, and 250 × 1.2 = 300. Taking 20% off £300 gives £240, which lands short.

pages.name: Undo a 25% rise
pages.task: A price went up 25% to £100. What percentage cut takes it back to where it started?
pages.why: It started at 100 ÷ 1.25 = £80, so the cut is £20. £20 is 20% of £100, because the cut is worked from the bigger amount. A 25% cut would land at £75.

pages.name: Drag back to 100%
pages.task: A cable run was cut 20% to 48 m. Drag the end to the run before, then pick it.
pages.why: The run before is 100%, and 48 m is 80% of it. 48 ÷ 0.8 = 60 m, and 60 × 0.8 = 48 checks it. Adding 20% of 48 m gives 57.6 m, too little.

pages.name: A 4% drop
pages.task: A supply has dropped 4% to 384 V. What was it before the drop?
pages.why: A 4% drop leaves 96%, so 384 V is 96% of the supply. 384 ÷ 0.96 = 400 V. Adding 4% of 384 V gives 399.36 V, close but short, as the drop was 4% of the bigger voltage.

pages.name: 8% added
pages.task: A part costs £54 with 8% added on. Which sum gives the price before?
pages.why: 8% added makes 108%, which is 1.08, so divide by 1.08. 54 ÷ 1.08 = £50, and 50 × 1.08 = 54. Dividing by 1.8 would undo an 80% rise.

pages.name: Up, down, back
pages.task: Put it together. A price went up 10%, then down 10%, and is now £99. What was it at the start?
pages.why: Up 10% then down 10% is 1.1 × 0.9 = 0.99, so £99 is 99% of the start. 99 ÷ 0.99 = £100. The two changes do not cancel.
